paper_metadata.title: Hybrid Quantum Classical Model for Enhanced Cross Border Financial Fraud Detection

summary: The paper presents a hybrid classical-quantum fraud-detection study comparing classical SVM with QSVM on cross-border transaction data using angle encoding, Z/ZZ feature maps, and a quantum kernel. It reports that the dataset includes 6 features (Transaction ID, Amount, Country Risk, Time of Day, Sender Blacklisted, Sender Age Days) and evaluates accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, false-positive rate, ROC, and confusion matrices, but no actual metric values, qubit counts, or circuit depths are given in the provided text.

experiments.description: Comparative fraud-detection experiment evaluating a classical SVM baseline against a quantum support vector machine (QSVM) on cross-border financial transaction data, using quantum feature maps and a quantum kernel in a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline.

algorithm.variant: QSVM with quantum feature maps (Z and ZZ maps) and quantum kernel evaluation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical transaction features are standardized, reduced with PCA to at most four components, normalized to [0, π], and encoded as rotation angles on qubits; entangling CNOT gates are used to create correlated quantum features.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of transactions into genuine (0) vs fraud (1) by maximizing separation in quantum feature space; quantum kernel SVM classification objective.

problem_instance.description: Cross-border financial fraud detection on a transaction dataset with features including transaction amount, country risk, time of day, sender blacklisted status, sender age in days, and binary fraud label.

dataset_specification.description: Columns: Transaction ID, Amount, Country Risk, Time of Day, Sender Blacklisted, Sender Age Days, Label. Time of Day encoded Day/Night to 0/1. PCA reduces features to at most four components.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Data validation for required columns; categorical encoding of Time of Day; filtering by transaction cohorts; standardization to zero mean and unit variance; PCA dimensionality reduction to at most four components; feature normalization to [0, π].
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparative evaluation of classical SVM vs QSVM using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, false-positive rate, ROC curves, and confusion matrices.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Standardization, PCA, categorical encoding, feature normalization, cohort filtering
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Performance metrics computation; ROC and confusion matrix visualization

speedup_claims.conditions: comparative empirical study on cross-border financial transaction data using a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper discusses potential quantum advantages qualitatively, but does not report a quantified speedup or asymptotic improvement.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not enough quantitative data reported; paper mentions simulator-based testing and hardware constraints qualitatively, but gives no qubit count, circuit depth, or asymptotic complexity.
limiting_factors: No reported numerical results for accuracy, precision, recall, F1, false-positive rate, or AUC

notes: Hardware type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the QSVM uses PennyLane with a default qubit simulator and does not name a real QPU device.
Number of qubits and circuit depth are not explicitly reported in the provided text; only that features are mapped to qubits and the circuit includes entangling CNOT gates.
